content.text: {"title":"Ishika's Green Leaf Discovery","gradeSubjectTag":"Class 5 · Science · Why Leaves Are Green","readMinutes":2,"scenes":[{"label":"hook","text":"Ishika was sitting in her grandmother's garden on a sunny afternoon, looking at all the different coloured flowers. 'Why are the roses red and the marigolds orange?' she asked. 'But look at the leaves around them — they are all green. Why is that?'"},{"label":"problem","text":"Grandmother smiled. 'That is a wonderful question. Let me show you something.' She held up a leaf to the sunlight. 'Leaves need to make food for the plant, just like your mother makes food for you. But how do they do it?'"},{"label":"mathMoment","text":"'Inside each leaf,' said Grandmother, 'there is a green colour called chlorophyll. This chlorophyll catches the sunlight and uses it to make food from air and water. The green colour is very special because it can catch red and blue light from the sun best, but it bounces back the green light. That is why we see the leaf as green — the green light bounces into our eyes!'"},{"label":"wrapUp","text":"Ishika picked a leaf and held it up to the sun. Now she understood — the leaf was green not by accident, but because green was the perfect colour to help the plant eat sunlight and grow strong. Every green leaf in the garden was busy working, and she had solved the mystery."}],"visual":null,"equations":[],"tryTogether":{"question":"You see a plant with yellow leaves instead of green ones. What might be wrong with how that plant is making its food?","answer":"The plant may not have enough chlorophyll, or it is not getting enough sunlight to work properly."},"parentPrompt":"Ask Ishika to find 3 different shades of green leaf around your home and compare them."}
